place.title: Place {ref} (real-time clock)
place.text: Push {ref}'s 6 header pins into column f, one pin per row: 32K into {hole.32k}, SQW into {hole.sqw}, SCL into {hole.scl}, SDA into {hole.sda}, VCC into {hole.vcc}, GND into {hole.gnd}. The board stands up with its chips facing the centre channel; its coin cell is on the back.
place.tip: Read the labels printed next to the pins. If yours are in another order, follow the labels, not the picture. 32K and SQW get no wire.

why: {ref} counts the time with its own very steady crystal and keeps counting on its coin cell when the Pico is off. The Pico reads the time over I2C: SDA (data) and SCL (clock).

wire.ground: This connects {ref}'s GND pin to ground.
wire.power: This powers {ref} from 3.3 V, so its I2C lines stay at the Pico's 3.3 V.
wire.i2c_sda: {pin} is the I2C{bus} data line (SDA): the Pico and {ref} send their bytes on this wire.
wire.i2c_scl: {pin} is the I2C{bus} clock line (SCL): it sets the pace for the data on SDA.
